subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: What durable Mattermost interaction-signing secret model should replace bot-token-derived signing before the linked fix lands?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the repair changes a channel security boundary and may add credential/config, docs, and upgrade behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use a per-account stored secret
options.body: Generate or require a durable per-account interaction secret, persist it through the plugin-owned credential/config path, update docs, and prove old bot-token-derived forgeries fail while valid buttons still work.

options.title: Require explicit configured secret only
options.body: Avoid automatic generation and make operators configure the interaction secret, trading less migration logic for more setup friction and possible button-delivery regressions.

options.title: Keep bot-token derivation
options.body: Accept the current coupling between Mattermost API credentials and interaction signing, which leaves this reported security boundary unchanged.

recommendation.title: Use a per-account stored secret
recommendation.body: Generate or require a durable per-account interaction secret, persist it through the plugin-owned credential/config path, update docs, and prove old bot-token-derived forgeries fail while valid buttons still work.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original Mattermost interactive-buttons PR and authored adjacent callback security/reachability work on the same surface.
